clauses.current_legal_basis: The held original text of EO 11267 (31 FR 807) states no end for this clause. The three selected machine searches (current-law:usc: U.S. Code release point 119-121 through 2026-10-09, with laws of 2026-10-10 to 2026-10-14 not reflected, a stated limit; current-law:ecfr: eCFR as of 2026-10-14; later-events:ofr_catalog: Federal Register executive-order catalog disposition notes) were read with their coverage notes and carry no coverage warning; the eCFR search records a hit at 8 CFR 252.5, which cites this order as authority for special procedures for deserters from Spanish or Greek ships of war; that regulation text is a machine lead whose text is not a packet source and is corroboration only, and the catalog search records no disposition note. The clause therefore continues on the original text, checked through 2026-10-14.
clauses.reason: The order designates the Attorney General, and such other officers and employees of the Executive Branch as the Attorney General may from time to time specify, as the competent national authorities of the United States under Article XXIV of the Treaty of Friendship and General Relations between the United States and Spain (33 Stat. 2105, 2117), and directs them to fulfill the obligations the United States assumed under Article XXIV in the manner and form there prescribed. It has no end date or ending condition of its own and nothing held amends, revokes or supersedes it, so it is operative on 2026-10-14.

research_rationale:
basis_pattern: original_plus_bounded_search. EO 11267 (signed 1966-01-19; 31 FR 807; official Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11267.txt, read in full) designates the Attorney General and his designees as the competent national authorities of the United States under Article XXIV of the Treaty of Friendship and General Relations with Spain and directs them to fulfill the obligations assumed under that Article. Identity: the heading of Executive Order 11267 on implementing the Treaty of Friendship and General Relations between the United States and Spain at 31 FR 807, the title and the date agree with the register row. The dossier inventory has one clause covering the whole operative text (the designation and the directive to fulfill the Article XXIV obligations, which form one continuing designation); I confirmed it without correction. Own terms: the order has no end date or ending condition and no savings clause. Later instruments: a search of every held order text for the number 11267 finds only the order's own Federal Register copy, the 1989 codification snapshot, and 8 CFR 252.5 (held in two copies), which cites the order as current authority; the dossier chain has no event and lists no actor. No held text revokes, supersedes or amends it. The three selected machine searches (current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr, later-events:ofr_catalog) were read with their coverage notes, carry no coverage warning, and record 1, 1 and 0 hits for the order number respectively. Limit stated plainly: the continuing predicate rests on the held original text and the bounded searches (U.S. Code through 2026-10-09); the text of the treaty is not held, so I do not assert how the treaty's own continuation bears on the order beyond the absence of any held instrument ending it; 8 CFR 252.5 and 28 CFR 0.109 are leads that the Attorney General's functions under the order continue, not quoted because their text is not a packet source.
